taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew and Flora of North America treatments and native to Texas at state scale.
look_here_first: First inspect the UPPER surface of an upper leaf or white-margined bract. If it is conspicuously hairy, then check bract shape: snow-on-the-prairie has long, narrow linear to narrowly oblanceolate white-margined bracts. The white display is bract tissue, not petals.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays is documented at Purola and Travis by multiple UT specimens. No third exact project target-zone county is locked.

approval_exception.reason: Learner admission is independent from native-range certification; preserve the two-county HOLD.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia: milky latex; true flowers are highly reduced and grouped in a cyathium; the showy white structures here are bracts and gland appendages, not ordinary petals.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Annual, taprooted, erect to suberect herb, commonly about 40–110 cm tall.
morphology_keys.leaves: Cauline leaves narrowly obovate/elliptic to lanceolate; uppermost leaves and bracts develop conspicuous white margins.
morphology_keys.pubescence: Stems, leaves, bracts, inflorescence, and capsules are conspicuously pilose/villous; hairs may be several millimeters long.
morphology_keys.bracts: Largest showy bracts are long and narrow, typically linear to narrowly oblanceolate rather than broadly elliptic.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Small flower-like cyathia with usually 4–5 nectar glands bearing white petal-like appendages.
best_field_traits: erect annual, often conspicuously white-topped in late summer
long narrow linear to narrowly oblanceolate white-margined bracts
white showy structures are bracts/gland appendages, not petals
cyathia with 4–5 glands and white appendages
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against E. marginata, prioritize two characters together: upper-surface hairiness and bract width. E. bicolor is the narrow-and-hairy plant; E. marginata is generally the broader-and-glabrous-above plant.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia marginata: mostly glabrous above; hairs may occur elsewhere, especially lower surfaces/midrib

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia bicolor: linear to narrowly oblanceolate; long and narrow

comparisons.key_distinctions: Narrow white-margined bracts PLUS conspicuous upper-surface hairiness strongly favor E. bicolor. Do not use the amount of white, plant height, or habitat alone.
